Hi Sarah —

Really helpful summary — thanks. Quick read of the profile suggests this is a memory-first workload given the 30k windows and KV residency. High-level guidance up front:

- H100 (80GB) is the most straightforward single-SKU fit for native memory headroom at long context lengths; it keeps the KV cache and activations on-device and simplifies scheduling.
- A100 (40/80GB) can work for sharded/tiling approaches but requires more orchestration and typically increases p50 under load unless you dedicate more instances.
- L4 is attractive for non-longcontext inference (lighter prompts / preprocessing / embedding tasks) but will not meet the memory needs for full 30k sequences unless you offload/cache heavily.

I’ll attach a preliminary sizing spreadsheet (initial-sizing-estimate.xlsx) with two scenarios: conservative (H100-heavy) and hybrid (H100 + A100 + L4). Before I finalize, I want to loop in Dev for ops-level sizing and Kim for capacity/contract impact.

Quick proposal: schedule a short architecture call Monday to align on SLOs and cost envelope. If you need numbers for procurement now, the spreadsheet has ballpark monthly reserved capacity costs by SKU.

—Connor

Thanks for the ping. A few concrete ops notes based on the model profile: 

- Memory footprint: with a 30k token working set and a mid-sized decoder model, expect KV + activations to approach the 60–75GB range after warmup. That pushes you toward H100 80GB (or aggregated A100-80GB if you plan multi-card sharding).
- Throughput/latency: A single H100-80GB instance can serve moderate qps with single-request latency within your p50 target when combined with prefix kv-cache and async batching tuned to small batches (2–4 tokens). But sustained 12 qps may require multiple slots; plan for N+1 redundancy.
- Hybrid fallback pattern: prefer primary H100 pool for long-context inference; maintain a mid-tier A100 pool for sharded batch work and an L4 pool for pre/post-processing and cheap embedding calls. Use smart routing: route long-context requests to H100; if H100 queue > threshold, degrade to A100 with partial context truncation AND a short-circuit policy to reduce context length (e.g., 20% truncation) before hitting L4 fallback.
- Cost optimization: aggressive quantization plus KV compression can reduce footprint ~15–25% at modest quality cost. We should run a quick eval on a small prompt set.

I added a quick ops worksheet in the sizing spreadsheet showing required slots for 12 qps steady (assume 40% cache hit effectiveness) and peak headroom. Happy to present the numbers in the call.

—Dev

Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU choice — final recommended runbook and next steps

Sarah —

Thanks — here’s a pragmatic runbook we recommend for EDGE-8812 to balance memory needs, latency SLOs, and cost: 

1) Initial reserved mix (Month 1 committed):
   - H100-80GB: 6 instances (primary long-context pool)
   - A100-80GB: 3 instances (mid-tier sharded work / fallthrough)
   - L4: 2 instances (pre/post, embeddings, cheap fallbacks)
   Rationale: this gives ~N+1 redundancy for steady 12 qps with modest burst headroom and a clear routing policy.

2) Canary and ramp plan:
   - Week 1: Canary on 2 H100 + 1 A100 behind a staging traffic split (5%–10% traffic). Validate prompt set and run quantization eval.
   - Week 2–3: Gradual ramp to 60% production traffic; monitor p50/p95 and cache hit.
   - Week 4: Flip to primary + scale to full reserved mix if metrics stable.

3) Fallback policy (automated):
   - If H100 queue latency > 300ms and backlog > 8 requests, route new long-context requests to A100 with forced 20% context truncation.
   - If A100 cannot keep up, route lightweight requests to L4 and return degrade-to-summary response for longest contexts.

4) Cost delta (ballpark):
   - H100-only committed: baseline X (see spreadsheet).
   - Proposed hybrid (above): ~35% lower monthly committed cost vs H100-only in our estimate. Exact figure depends on reserved term and cloud SKU pricing — see initial-sizing-estimate.xlsx for line items.

5) Action items / next steps:
   - Connor/Dev: run a quick 1k-sample eval to confirm quality impact of 20% truncation and quantization knobs.
   - Marissa: prepare draft reserved contract (term options) and DocuSign link for procurement.
   - Sarah: confirm whether you want us to proceed with Week 1 canary scheduling.

I’ll open a short call to walk the team through the spreadsheet. If that sounds good, we can convert the proposed mix into a reserved capacity agreement (DocuSign link: https://docusign.example/EDGE-8812-reserve).

Thanks — talk soon.

—Connor
